findings.title: Test named for docType-value enforcement asserts nothing about it
findings.description: The test name and comments say it proves the `docType` `values` constraint is enforced. It doesn't. Every assertion is `toHaveLength(0)`: valid `devlog`, valid `gate-evidence`, and an unknown docType that skips validation. No case feeds a mismatched docType into a schema and expects a finding. The test would still pass if the `values` constraints on the three new schemas were deleted. Either remove it, or add a case that can fail. For example, call `validateFrontmatter` with the `devlog` schema against `docType: 'gate-evidence'` and expect a finding. That needs a way to select the schema explicitly. The test as written gives false confidence, which the project's parser-test rules warn against.
findings.location: packages/core/tests/schema/frontmatterSchema.test.ts (test 'a wrong docType literal is still caught by the value-constraint logic')

findings.title: Presentation logic duplicated from `cf check`
findings.description: `SEVERITY_ICON`, the severity-to-colour selection, the findings loop, and the fix-log lookup repeat the same logic in `packages/cli/src/commands/check.ts`. `check.ts` defines an identical `SEVERITY_ICON` at line 25. Two copies of the same finding renderer will drift. Extract a shared helper, for example in `output/`, for the icon map and per-finding rendering. The map is also typed `Record<string, string>` with a `?? '?'` fallback. That is a silent placeholder, and a typed severity key would make it exhaustive.

findings.title: JSON output omits post-fix state and is loosely typed
findings.description: `totalFindings`, `errors`, `warnings` and `findings` always describe the pre-fix findings. With `--fix`, the process can exit 1 because `remaining` is non-empty, yet the JSON has no `remaining` count. Consumers have to derive it as `totalFindings - fixed`. The payload is also built as `Record<string, unknown>` and mutated conditionally. A named interface with optional fix fields would give the documented shape a type contract. The `--json` tests only check selected keys.

findings.title: `fixLog` lookup is keyed by filePath and field
findings.description: `fixLog.find` matches on `filePath` and `field`. If one file ever produced two findings for the same field, both would display the first entry's before/after. This is unlikely given per-document schema findings, so I'm noting it and not flagging it.

findings.title: Exit-code and error-handling design
findings.description: Adding the `exitCode = 1` parameter to `handleError` is backward compatible. The per-fix `catch` collects the error message into `fixErrors`, marks the finding as still broken, and reports it in both output modes. That handling is sound, and the exit codes (0 clean, 1 findings or fix failures, 2 operational errors) are covered by tests. The new schemas for `review-resolution`, `gate-evidence` and `devlog` are well documented, and the reason for omitting `dateUpdated` is recorded in the schema comment.
